note: Adapted from the original description of Termes gratus by Sjöstedt (1900), which includes a Latin diagnosis and a German description; only the alate is described, soldier and worker not recorded; the names of two allied species used for comparison are illegible owing to OCR damage and are therefore referred to as 'allied species'; fragmentary figures such as wing width are not recorded; specimen records are not translated.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Wings dark brown, with a dark smoky tinge, the wing surface therefore appearing darker. The species is closest to two allied species: compared with one of them, it is smaller and its wings show a more pronounced dark smoky tinge. Compared with the other, it is smaller and slightly paler, and more notably the middle of the pronotum lacks a circular fovea — in that allied species the middle of the anterior pronotal margin is distinctly notched, whereas in the present species the middle is not concave at all; the wing colour is also paler. Compared with two other allied species, it differs in the darker wings and in the distance between ocellus and compound eye, which almost exceeds the length of the ocellar diameter. Wing expanse 65–70 mm, body length with wings 35–38 mm, wing length 29–32 mm, body length including head 19 mm.
